  SUBROUTINE write_checkpoint(fname,iter,etot,conv)

subtasks.title: Develop POSIX signal C wrapper (signal_wrap.c) and public header
subtasks.description: Create a small C source file wrapping the POSIX signal(3) API so that Fortran code can register its own handlers for SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 via ISO_C_BINDING C_FUNPTRs.
subtasks.details:
• File: src/signal_wrap.c (or Modules/signal_wrap.c depending on layout).  
• Include <signal.h> and <stdint.h>.  
• Expose two extern "C" functions with BIND(C)-compatible names:  
    void c_set_usr1_handler(void (*f)(int));  
    void c_set_usr2_handler(void (*f)(int));  
  Each stores the passed function pointer in a static and calls signal(SIGUSR1/2, f).  
• Provide a no-op default stub to avoid null pointers before Fortran installs its handlers.  
• Add signal_wrap.h exporting the prototypes (not strictly required by Fortran but useful for C unit tests).  
• Modify build system (make.inc) to compile signal_wrap.c and add it to the object list (e.g., OBJS += signal_wrap.o).  
• Compilation flags: -std=c99, ensure no name mangling (extern "C" if compiled as C++).
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a stand-alone C program that registers a dummy handler through c_set_usr1_handler, send itself SIGUSR1 with raise(), assert handler executed (e.g., increments volatile global). Build in CI with -fsanitize=address/undefined.

subtasks.title: Create checkpoint_manager.f90 skeleton with global flags and public API stubs
subtasks.description: Add Modules/checkpoint_manager.f90 containing module definition, global request flags, public interfaces and empty bodies for all advertised subroutines so the codebase can compile early.
subtasks.details:
• MODULE checkpoint_manager  
    USE ISO_C_BINDING  
    PRIVATE  
    PUBLIC :: install_signal_handlers, write_checkpoint, load_checkpoint, write_status_snapshot, soft_pause_requested, snapshot_requested  
    LOGICAL, VOLATILE :: soft_pause_requested = .FALSE., snapshot_requested = .FALSE.  
    INTERFACE  
       SUBROUTINE c_set_usr1_handler(f) BIND(C,NAME="c_set_usr1_handler")  
         IMPORT :: C_FUNPTR  
         TYPE(C_FUNPTR), VALUE :: f  
       END SUBROUTINE  
       SUBROUTINE c_set_usr2_handler(f) BIND(C,NAME="c_set_usr2_handler")  
         IMPORT :: C_FUNPTR  
         TYPE(C_FUNPTR), VALUE :: f  
       END SUBROUTINE  
    END INTERFACE  
    CONTAINS  
      SUBROUTINE install_signal_handlers() ; END  
      SUBROUTINE write_checkpoint(fname,iter,etot,conv) ; END  
      SUBROUTINE load_checkpoint(fname) ; END  
      SUBROUTINE write_status_snapshot(iter,etot,forces,stress) ; END  
 END MODULE checkpoint_manager
subtasks.testStrategy: Re-run full project build; ensure linkage with signal_wrap.o succeeds and module exports expected symbols via nm or objdump.

subtasks.title: Implement install_signal_handlers logic and Fortran signal callbacks
subtasks.description: Fill in install_signal_handlers() to bridge Fortran handlers with the C wrapper, define the actual handler subroutines that flip the module’s VOLATILE flags, and verify runtime signal delivery.
subtasks.details:
• In checkpoint_manager.f90 add:  
   SUBROUTINE handle_soft_pause_signal(sig) BIND(C) ; USE ISO_C_BINDING ; INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: sig ; soft_pause_requested = .TRUE. ; END  
   SUBROUTINE handle_snapshot_signal(sig) BIND(C) ; USE ISO_C_BINDING ; INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: sig ; snapshot_requested = .TRUE. ; END  
• Within install_signal_handlers():  
   TYPE(C_FUNPTR) :: fp1, fp2  
   fp1 = C_FUNLOC(handle_soft_pause_signal)  
   fp2 = C_FUNLOC(handle_snapshot_signal)  
   CALL c_set_usr1_handler(fp1)  
   CALL c_set_usr2_handler(fp2)  
• Ensure VOLATILE attribute on flags so they are visible across async signal contexts.  
• Update compiler flags (e.g., -fno-omit-frame-pointer, -pthread if needed).  
• Document that install_signal_handlers() must be invoked early in program start-up.

subtasks.title: Implement checkpoint read/write routines with versioned binary format
subtasks.description: Complete write_checkpoint() and load_checkpoint() to persist solver state to an unformatted sequential file, including a version tag for forward compatibility.
subtasks.details:
• Define INTEGER, PARAMETER :: chkpt_version = 1.  
• write_checkpoint(fname,iter,etot,conv):  
  OPEN(NEWUNIT=iu,FILE=fname,STATUS='REPLACE',ACCESS='SEQUENTIAL',FORM='UNFORMATTED')  
  WRITE(iu) chkpt_version  
  WRITE(iu) iter, etot, conv  
  ! Extend with REAL*8 arrays (forces, stress, etc.) when available  
  CLOSE(iu).  
• load_checkpoint(fname):  
  OPEN(NEWUNIT=iu,FILE=fname,STATUS='OLD',ACCESS='SEQUENTIAL',FORM='UNFORMATTED')  
  READ(iu) ver ; IF (ver /= chkpt_version) STOP 'Incompatible checkpoint'  
  READ(iu) iter, etot, conv  
  CLOSE(iu)  
• Add error trapping with IOSTAT and convert to module-local error codes.  
• Use flush(iu) or CLOSE action='KEEP' to guarantee data written.  
• Provide helper INTERNAL subroutine safe_open().
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test writes a checkpoint, immediately reads it back, compares all scalar values with ASSERT_EQ.  Run under valgrind to confirm no leaks or invalid memory.  Fallback path: attempt to read a deliberately corrupted version tag and assert graceful failure.

subtasks.title: Implement write_status_snapshot() utility, directory handling, and full integration tests
subtasks.description: Add human-readable snapshot writer, ensure directory creation via SYSTEM('mkdir -p …'), and assemble a comprehensive test suite that exercises signals, I/O, and memory safety.
subtasks.details:
• write_status_snapshot(iter,etot,forces,stress):  
  CHARACTER(LEN=*), PARAMETER :: dir='snapshots'  
  CALL SYSTEM('mkdir -p ' // trim(dir))  
  WRITE(filename,'(A,I0.6)') dir//'/snap_',iter,'.txt'  
  OPEN(NEWUNIT=iu,FILE=filename,STATUS='REPLACE',FORM='FORMATTED')  
  WRITE(iu,*) 'Iteration',iter  
  WRITE(iu,*) 'Etot',etot  
  IF (SIZE(forces)>0) WRITE(iu,*) 'Forces',forces  
  IF (SIZE(stress)>0) WRITE(iu,*) 'Stress',stress  
  CLOSE(iu)  
• At program main loop, caller can poll snapshot_requested and invoke this subroutine.  
• Extend make.inc test target to build test_signal_driver and a new test_checkpoint_io executable.  
• CI:   
   – Run tests on Linux & macOS.  
   – Use timeout to ensure checkpoint write < 2× baseline final write.  
   – Use valgrind/asan job for memory checking.  
• Documentation: update README and developer guide with usage instructions and environment notes (POSIX-only).
subtasks.testStrategy:
Integration script:  
  1) Start test_driver that installs handlers and enters compute loop.  
  2) Send SIGUSR2; wait; verify snapshots/<file> exists and contains correct iteration.  
  3) Send SIGUSR1; driver detects soft_pause_requested=.TRUE. and exits after checkpoint write.  
  4) Restart driver with --restart; verify it loads checkpoint and continues iterations.  
  All checks performed automatically in CI workflow.

subtasks.title: Implement soft-pause handling and graceful shutdown
subtasks.description: Add logic so that if local_soft is .TRUE. when entering an iteration, the code writes a checkpoint at the END of that iteration and exits via stop_run(.FALSE.).
subtasks.details:
• In main SCF loop declare logical :: pause_after_iter = .FALSE.
• Immediately after CALL handle_signal_requests set pause_after_iter = soft_pause_requested (read once more in CRITICAL).
• At very end of the iteration (just before END DO or cycle increment):
   IF(pause_after_iter) THEN
      fname = generate_checkpoint_filename()
      CALL write_checkpoint(fname, iter, etot, conv)
      IF (ionode) WRITE(io_global,*) "Soft pause requested – checkpoint written to",TRIM(fname)
      !$OMP CRITICAL(clear_soft)
      soft_pause_requested = .FALSE.
      !$OMP END CRITICAL(clear_soft)
      CALL stop_run(.FALSE.)
   END IF
• Ensure stop_run import via USE io_global or existing module.

subtasks.title: Implement suggest_kpoint_grid()
subtasks.description: Code the k-point grid suggestion algorithm based on reciprocal lattice norms and target spacing as described in the PRD reference.
subtasks.details:
• In parameter_optimization.f90 implement FUNCTION suggest_kpoint_grid(cell, spacing) RESULT(grid(3)) where spacing = 2π / cutoff_k.
• Extract lattice vectors from cell%alat, cell%bm.
• Compute reciprocal lattice vectors b1,b2,b3 and their norms.
• For each direction i: n_i = MAX(1, NINT(norm(b_i)/spacing)).
• Ensure n_i are odd when cell has inversion symmetry if optimize_kpoints%flags%require_gamma_centered.
• Emit VERBOSE output when io_global%ionode.
• Return integer array grid(3).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit: Silicon conventional cell (a=5.43 Å) expecting 6×6×6 grid for 0.15 Å⁻¹ spacing; assert equality. Edge cases: 1D chain (large a,b) should yield 1×1×N.

subtasks.title: Implement test_cutoff_convergence()
subtasks.description: Create routine that loops over kinetic-energy cutoffs (30→120 Ry) running single-point SCF in dry-run mode until total-energy change ΔE falls below target_accuracy.
subtasks.details:
• Implement FUNCTION test_cutoff_convergence(input_state, opt) RESULT(best_cutoff).
• Loop cutoff = 30,40,…,120 Ry while iter ≤ opt%max_iterations.
• For each cutoff: CALL scf_driver(input_state, cutoff, dry_run=.TRUE., energy=e(i)).
• After first step, compute ΔE = ABS(e(i)-e(i-1)); EXIT when ΔE < opt%target_accuracy.
• Return cutoff that satisfied criterion; if none, return last tested and flag warning.
• Store energies and cutoffs in local arrays; if io_global%ionode write a mini-table to output file.
subtasks.testStrategy: Mock scf_driver with deterministic function E(cutoff)=E0+1/cutoff^2 to avoid heavy computation; verify best_cutoff ≈ sqrt(1/target_accuracy) within tolerance. Test termination on both satisfied and unsatisfied cases.

subtasks.title: Implement optimize_parameters() orchestrator
subtasks.description: Combine k-point and cutoff optimisations under a single PUBLIC interface, update global simulation parameters, and respect SERIAL-only execution constraint.
subtasks.details:
• Implement SUBROUTINE optimize_parameters(input_state, opt, out_grid, out_cutoff).
• IF(opt%optimize_kpoints) CALL suggest_kpoint_grid() and overwrite k_points input variables (kpoint_grid, kpoint_shift).
• IF(opt%optimize_cutoff) CALL test_cutoff_convergence() and overwrite ecutwfc/ecutrho (ecutrho=4*ecutwfc default).
• Perform validity checks: throw error if existing k_points defined with automatic optimisation.
• Wrap the whole routine with IF(.NOT.is_mpi_enabled()) to enforce serial-only; otherwise PRINT warning and RETURN without changes.
• Propagate chosen parameters to subsequent setup routines via USEd common modules or by updating input_state.
• Provide verbose summary block printed once with chosen grid and cutoff.

subtasks.title: Implement interactive prompt and enforcement logic

subtasks.details:

     IF(.NOT.force_pp) THEN
         IF(isatty(0)) THEN
             WRITE(*,*) "Use recommended PP '",TRIM(recommended_name),"'? (y/n)"
             READ(*,*) answer
             IF(answer=='y' .OR. answer=='Y') THEN
                 CALL swap_pseudopotential(recommended_name)
             ENDIF
         ELSE

     ENDIF

subtasks.title: Define configuration schema and default INI template
subtasks.description: Create a formal list of configurable keys, their default values, data types, and acceptable ranges/severities for each sanity check. Provide a default INI string that will be written to ~/.qe/config.ini on first run.
subtasks.details:

subtasks.title: Implement compact INI parser/serializer with optional INIH C backend
subtasks.description: Provide a Fortran-visible API capable of reading an INI file into a mapping structure and writing it back. Prefer a pure Fortran fallback using READ(unit,*) and simple section/key scanning, and enable optional linking against INIH via ISO_C_BINDING for performance.
subtasks.details:
1. Define TYPE ini_kv_pair (CHARACTER(:), CHARACTER(:)) and TYPE ini_section containing an allocatable array of pairs.
2. Implement read_ini_pure(unit, sections) that line-scans, trims, ignores comments (# and ;) and fills data structures.
3. Add BUILD flag USE_INIH; if defined, provide INTERFACE to inih C functions ini_parse_string / ini_parse_file; wrap them into read_ini_inih.
4. Provide generic read_ini() that dispatches depending on build flag.
5. Implement write_ini(unit, sections) with aligned “key = value” formatting, preserving order.
6. Expose PUBLIC: load_ini(path, sections), save_ini(path, sections), get_value(section,key,default), set_value(section,key,val).
subtasks.testStrategy: Round-trip test: load default template, modify one key, save, reload, assert equality. Build matrix for both pure and INIH back-ends under CI.

subtasks.title: Develop sanity_config.f90 module

subtasks.title: Implement individual sanity check routines in sanity_checks.f90
subtasks.description: Write self-contained functions to evaluate each physical sanity criterion, using thresholds from sanity_config module.
subtasks.details:
1. MODULE sanity_checks; USE sanity_config.
2. For each check:
   a) check_atomic_distances(structure) -> returns severity & message; compute pairwise distances, compare with distance.min.
   b) check_cell_angles(cell) -> evaluate angles vs angle.max/min.
   c) check_isolated_atoms(structure) -> graph analysis within isolation.radius.
   d) check_symmetry_break(structure) -> compare nominal lattice symmetry with atomic positions tolerance.
3. Define TYPE san_result (severity, message, suggestion).
4. Provide PUBLIC perform_all_checks(structure, cell, results(:)).
subtasks.testStrategy: Craft small mock structures: (i) two atoms at 0.3 Å, expect critical; (ii) 60° cell, expect warning; (iii) isolated single atom, etc. Assert severity matches expected config.

subtasks.title: Create run_all_checks orchestrator with interactive prompt and force bypass

4. For warning, prompt user via READ(*,*) unless prompt_on_warning=.false.; respect batch/non-interactive mode by checking INPUT_UNIT==F.
5. Respect global config log_level when printing.
6. Return logical so caller can decide to exit or proceed.

subtasks.title: Wire sanity-check execution flow into setup based on CLI flags
subtasks.description: Call load_sanity_config, execute run_all_checks(), and control continuation/early exit according to --ignore-sanity-checks, --sanity-checks-only, and --force.

• ELSE CALL run_all_checks(can_continue) from sanity_checks module.
• When can_continue=.FALSE. AND .NOT. force_checks THEN gracefully STOP with informative banner.
• If checks_only .TRUE. THEN after successful checks (regardless of force/ignore) STOP without entering the normal computation loop.
• Make sure force_checks overrides can_continue but not checks_only.
• Return proper exit status codes (0 success, 2 aborted by failed sanity).
subtasks.testStrategy:
End-to-end:
1. pw.x --sanity-checks-only input → program terminates after checks.
2. pw.x --ignore-sanity-checks → no check output.
3. Introduce failing geometry, run without --force → program exits with status 2; run with --force continues.

subtasks.title: Implement job control REST endpoints & process manager
subtasks.description: Add /run, /pause and /snapshot POST routes and internal logic to start an external QE calculation, persist its PID and deliver POSIX signals for pause/resume & snapshot handling.
subtasks.details:
1. Create ProcessManager class in qe_gui_server.py with methods:
   • `start(cmd:list)` → stores subprocess.Popen handle, writes PID to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/qe_job.pid`.
   • `pause()` → `os.kill(pid, signal.SIGUSR1)`.
   • `snapshot()` → `os.kill(pid, signal.SIGUSR2)`.
   • `status()` → dict with running flag, returncode, start_time.
2. Wire Flask routes:
   • POST /run {"cmd": "pw.x -in input.in"} calls ProcessManager.start(). Reject if a job is already running.
   • POST /pause calls pause(); success 202.
   • POST /snapshot calls snapshot(); success 202.
   • GET /status returns ProcessManager.status() JSON.
3. Capture stdout/stderr with `subprocess.Popen(..., text=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=STDOUT)`; start a background Thread that reads lines and appends to a ring buffer for later WebSocket emission.
4. Ensure graceful cleanup: register atexit handler to terminate orphan processes.
5. Guard POSIX-only code under `if os.name != 'posix': abort(501, "Signals not supported on this platform")`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Pytest using monkeypatch to replace subprocess.Popen with a dummy process object that records received signals; verify: POST /run returns 201, POST /pause delivers SIGUSR1, POST /snapshot delivers SIGUSR2, and status reflects state transitions.

subtasks.title: Sanity check execution & result parsing
subtasks.description: Provide /check POST route that runs QE sanity pre-checks, parses their output by severity and returns structured JSON conforming to an explicit schema.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test feeds sample stdout lines via monkeypatch to run_sanity_checks() and asserts JSON matches schema. Integration test: POST /check returns correct counts given mocked subprocess output.

subtasks.title: WebSocket broadcasting & liveness monitoring
subtasks.description: Stream live job output and heartbeat information to connected clients using Flask-SocketIO, backed by pythonping for host reachability.
subtasks.details:
1. Extend ProcessManager thread created in subtask 2 to emit each captured stdout line via `socketio.emit('job_output', {'line': line})`.
2. Add namespace `/events`; on `connect` send current status immediately.
3. Create PingMonitor Thread that every 5 s runs `pythonping(ping_target, count=1)`; emit `socketio.emit('host_ping', {'alive': True, 'latency_ms': ...})`.
4. Tie status events: when ProcessManager detects process end, emit `socketio.emit('job_finished', status_dict)`.
5. Update REST endpoints to also broadcast `job_started`, `job_paused`, `snapshot_taken` events so UI stays in sync.
6. Document message contract in README (event names, payload JSON).
subtasks.testStrategy: Use python-socketio test client: start server in background, connect, trigger /run with dummy process, assert reception of 'job_started' and continuous 'job_output' lines, kill job and assert 'job_finished'.

subtasks.title: Deployment packaging & systemd user service
subtasks.description: Finalize production deployment artefacts: systemd unit, launch script and end-to-end tests.
subtasks.details:
1. Create GUI/systemd/qe-gui-server.service:
   [Unit]
   Description=Quantum Espresso GUI backend
   After=network.target
   [Service]
   ExecStart=/usr/bin/env poetry run python -m qe_gui_server
   Restart=on-failure
   WorkingDirectory=%h/projects/qe-gui
   Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
   [Install]
   WantedBy=default.target
2. Provide install script `install_service.sh` that copies the file to `~/.config/systemd/user/` and runs `systemctl --user enable --now qe-gui-server.service`.
3. Add README section with instructions for both Poetry and requirements.txt users, list open port, firewall notes.
4. Build automation: GitHub Action (or Make target) that runs `pytest`, lints with flake8 and, on success, packages a tarball containing source + schema + unit file.
5. End-to-end test script `tests/e2e_backend.py`: launches server via `subprocess.Popen`, waits on /health, executes the complete REST workflow (check → run → pause → snapshot) against a mock calc, then terminates server.
6. Ensure CI passes on Ubuntu-latest; mark SIGUSR* tests with `pytest.mark.skipif(os.name!='posix', ...)`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Manual: run `install_service.sh`, execute `systemctl --user status qe-gui-server` and curl /health. CI: e2e test must exit 0.
